This is one of the kindnesses of Allah, exalted is He, toward His creation: that He sends to them messengers from among them, speaking their languages, so that they may understand from them what is wanted of them and what they were sent with to them. As the Imam Ahmad said:

Waki' narrated to us, from 'Umar ibn Dharr, who said: Mujahid said, from Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has never sent a prophet except in the language of his people."^[Al-Musnad (5/158). Mujahid did not hear from Abu Dharr.]

And His saying: ﴿So Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills﴾ means: after the clarification and the establishment of proof against them, Allah, exalted is He, leaves astray whom He wills from the path of guidance, and guides whom He wills to the truth. ﴿And He is the Mighty﴾, whatever He wills comes to pass and whatever He does not will does not come to pass, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His actions, so He leaves astray whoever deserves to be led astray, and guides whoever is worthy of that.

This has been the custom of Allah with His creation: He never sent a prophet to a nation except that he spoke their language. Thus each prophet was specially charged with conveying his message to his own nation and not to others. Allah specially favoured Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah, the Messenger of Allah, with a message of universal scope to all mankind, as is established in the two Sahihs from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I have been given five things which were not given to any prophet before me: I was helped with terror (awe) over a distance of a month's journey; the earth has been made for me a place of prostration and a means of purification; spoils of war have been made lawful for me, though they were not lawful for anyone before me; I have been given the intercession; and every prophet used to be sent only to his own people, whereas I have been sent to all mankind."^[Sahih al-Bukhari (335) and Sahih Muslim (521).]

It has witnesses from many routes. And Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Say: O mankind, I am the Messenger of Allah to you all﴾ [al-A'raf: 158].

Allah says: "Just as We sent you, O Muhammad, and revealed the Book to you, that you may bring mankind, all of them, out of the darkness into the light, calling them to come out from the darknesses to the light, so too We sent Musa (Moses) with Our signs to the Children of Israel."

Mujahid said: "The signs here are the nine signs."

﴿That bring out your people from the darknesses﴾, meaning: We commanded him, saying to him, ﴿Bring out your people from the darknesses to the light﴾, meaning: call them to goodness, so that they may come out from the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance they were in, to the light of guidance and the insight of faith.

﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾, meaning: of His favours and blessings upon them, in bringing them out from the captivity of Pharaoh, and his domination, his oppression and his tyranny, and in saving them from their enemy, and splitting the sea for them, and shading them with the clouds, and sending down upon them the manna and the quails, and other blessings. Mujahid, Qatadah and others said this.

There has come concerning this a marfu' hadith (one traced directly to the Prophet ﷺ), which 'Abdullah ibn the Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated in the Musnad of his father, where he said: "Yahya ibn 'Abdullah, mawla (client) of the Banu Hashim, related to me: Muhammad ibn Aban al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, [from Ibn 'Abbas, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿And remind them of the Days of Allah﴾, he said: "With the blessings of Allah, blessed and exalted is He"]."

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] and Ibn Abi Hatim also narrated it through Muhammad ibn Aban, with the same chain. [Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/122) and Tafsir al-Tabari (16/522).] 'Abdullah, the son of Ahmad, also narrated it as a mawquf (one ending with a Companion) report [Zawa'id al-Musnad (5/122)], and this is more akin to being correct.

His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾, meaning: indeed in what We did for Our friends, the Children of Israel, when We rescued them from the hand of Pharaoh and saved them from the humiliating torment they were in, there is a lesson for every steadfast one (sabbar), i.e., in adversity, and grateful one (shakur), i.e., in ease. As Qatadah said: "What an excellent servant is the one who, when tested, is patient, and when given, is thankful."

Similarly, it has come in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "The affair of the believer is entirely wondrous. Allah does not decree for him any decree except that it is good for him. If adversity befalls him, he is patient, and that is good for him; and if ease befalls him, he is thankful, and that is good for him." [Sahih Muslim no. (2999), from the hadith of Suhayb (may Allah be pleased with him).]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 14, verse 6–8:

Allah, exalted is He, says, informing about Musa (Moses), when he reminded his people of the days of Allah among them and His blessings upon them, when He rescued them from the household of Fir'awn (Pharaoh), and from the torment and humiliation they inflicted upon them, when they used to slaughter whoever of their sons was found and leave their females alive. So Allah saved Bani Isra'il (the Children of Israel) from that, and this is a great blessing. Therefore He said: ﴿And in that was a great trial from your Lord﴾, meaning: a great blessing from Him upon you in that, which you are unable to give thanks for properly.

It has also been said: "And in what Fir'awn's people did to you of those deeds" ﴿is a trial﴾, meaning: a great test. It is possible that both are intended together, and Allah knows best, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We tested them with good things and bad things that they might return﴾ [Al-A'raf: 168].

* *

His saying: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed﴾ means: He announced to you and informed you of His promise to you. It is also possible that the meaning is: "And when your Lord swore and took an oath by His might, majesty and greatness," as He said: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst torment﴾ [Al-A'raf: 167].

* *

His saying [here]: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ means: If you are grateful for My blessing upon you, I will surely increase you from it. ﴿But if you deny, indeed, My punishment is severe﴾ means: if you deny the blessings, conceal them and reject them, and that is by their removal from them and His punishment of them for their disbelief in them.

It has come in a hadith: "Indeed, a servant is deprived of provision because of a sin that befalls him" (narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (5/80) and Ibn Majah in his Sunan, no. 90, from the hadith of Thawban, may Allah be pleased with him; al-Iraqi graded it hasan as cited in al-Zawaid of al-Busiri (1/61)).

In the Musnad: that a beggar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he gave him a date, but he disdained it and did not accept it. Then another passed by him and he gave it to him, and he accepted it and said: "A date from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" So he ordered for him forty dirhams, or as he said.

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad narrated to us, 'Umarah al-Saydalani narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas who said: A beggar came to the Prophet ﷺ, and he ordered that he be given a date, but he did not take it, or he was repelled by it. He said: And another came to him, and he ordered that he be given a date, and he said: "Glory be to Allah! A date from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ!" So he said to the slave girl: "Go to Umm Salamah and give him the forty dirhams that she has."

Imam Ahmad alone narrated it (al-Musnad (3/154)).

'Umarah ibn Zadhan: Ibn Hibban, Ahmad, and Ya'qub ibn Sufyan declared him trustworthy [in another narration: "Ahmad, Ya'qub ibn Sufyan and Ibn Hibban"]. Ibn Ma'in said: "Salih" (acceptable). Abu Zur'ah said: "There is no harm in him." Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is written down but not used as evidence; he is not firm." Al-Bukhari said: "He sometimes becomes confused in his hadith." And it is also narrated from Ahmad that he said: "Munkar (rejected) hadiths have been related from him." Abu Dawud said: "He is not of that standard." Al-Daraqutni weakened him, and Ibn 'Adi said: "There is no harm in him among those whose hadith is written."

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Musa said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ means: He is free of need of the gratitude of His servants, and He is the Praiseworthy, the One who is praised, even if whoever disbelieves disbelieves, as He said: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; but if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [Az-Zumar: 7], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need, and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6].

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dhar, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what he narrates from his Lord, mighty and majestic is He, that He said: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase in My kingdom anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease in My kingdom anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one open place and asked Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not decrease from My kingdom anything except as a needle decreases when it is put into the sea." So glorified and exalted is He, the Free of need, the Praiseworthy [Sahih Muslim, no. 2577].

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Musa said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on earth entirely, then indeed Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ means: He is free of need of the gratitude of His servants, and He is the Praiseworthy, the One who is praised, even if whoever disbelieves disbelieves, as He said: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; but if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [Az-Zumar: 7], and He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So they disbelieved and turned away, and Allah was free of need, and Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy﴾ [At-Taghabun: 6].

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dhar, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in what he narrates from his Lord, mighty and majestic is He, that He said: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase in My kingdom anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease in My kingdom anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, stood in one open place and asked Me, and I gave each person his request, that would not decrease from My kingdom anything except as a needle decreases when it is put into the sea." So glorified and exalted is He, the Free of need, the Praiseworthy [Sahih Muslim, no. 2577].

Ibn Jarir said: This is part of what Musa (Moses) said to his people [Tafsir al-Tabari (16/529)].

That is, [Musa was] reminding them of the Days of Allah, [meaning] His vengeance upon the nations that denied the messengers.

There is room for scrutiny in what Ibn Jarir said. The apparent meaning is that this is a fresh report from Allah Most High addressed to this Ummah, for it has been said that the story of 'Ad and Thamud is not in the Torah. If this were part of Musa's speech to his people, and he recounted those stories to them, then these two stories would undoubtedly be in the Torah, and Allah knows best. In sum, Allah Most High has related to us the account of the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud and others among the nations that denied the messengers, whose number none knows except Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, that is, with evident, dazzling and decisive arguments and evidences.

Ibn Ishaq related from Amr ibn Maymun, from Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) that he said, concerning the verse ﴿None knows them except Allah﴾: "The genealogists have lied."

Urwah ibn al-Zubayr said: "We have not found anyone who knows what lies beyond Ma'add ibn 'Adnan."

As for His saying ﴿and they put their hands into their mouths﴾, the commentators differed about its meaning. It has been said that it means they gestured toward the mouths of the messengers, ordering them to be silent, when they invited them to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

It has also been said: rather, they placed their hands upon their mouths in denial of them.

It has also been said: rather, it is an expression for their silence in response to the messengers.

Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b and Qatadah said: its meaning is that they denied them and returned their words back into their mouths.

Ibn Jarir said: its interpretation is that "fi" here carries the meaning of "ba" (with). He said: It has been heard from the Arabs, "adkhalaka Allahu bil-jannah" (meaning: fi al-jannah), and the poet said:

"And I am averse to her, [turning away] from Laqit and his clan, from Sinbis; I am not averse [to them]..."

He intends: "arghabu biha" (I desire her / I am drawn to her).

I say: What supports Mujahid's view is the explanation given by the complete statement: ﴿They said: "We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and we are truly in grave doubt about that to which you invite us."﴾ So it seems that this [and Allah knows best] is an explanation of the meaning of "returning their hands into their mouths."

Sufyan al-Thawri and Israil related from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah concerning His saying ﴿and they put their hands into their mouths﴾ that he said: "They bit them in rage."

Shu'bah related from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Hubayrah ibn Maryam, from Abdullah that he also said this. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam chose this view, and Ibn Jarir inclined to it, citing the saying of Allah Most High concerning the hypocrites: ﴿And when they are alone, they bite the tips of their fingers at you out of rage﴾ [Al 'Imran: 119].

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas: "When they heard the Book of Allah, they were amazed, and they returned their hands to their mouths."

And they said: ﴿We disbelieve in that with which you have been sent, and we are truly in grave doubt about that to which you invite us.﴾ They mean: "We will not believe you in what you have brought, for we have strong doubt about it."

Almighty Allah informs of the dispute that took place between the disbelievers and their messengers. When their peoples confronted them with doubt about what they had brought them, namely worshipping Allah alone, without partner, the messengers said: ﴿Is there doubt about Allah?﴾

This may bear two meanings. The first: Is there doubt about His existence? The innate nature (fitrah) bears witness to His existence and is disposed to acknowledge Him, for acknowledging Him is necessary in sound natures. Yet doubt and confusion may afflict some of them, so they need to reflect on the evidence that leads to His existence. For this reason the messengers said to them, guiding them to the way of knowing Him, that He is ﴿Creator of the heavens and the earth﴾, who created them and originated them without a prior pattern. The signs of their being originated, created and subjected are manifest in them, so they must have a maker, and He is Allah, there is no god but Him, the Creator of everything, its God and its Sovereign.

The second meaning of their words ﴿Is there doubt about Allah?﴾ is: Is there doubt about His divinity and His being singled out as the one deserving worship? He is the Creator of all existing things, and none deserves worship but Him, alone, without partner. For most nations acknowledged the Maker, but they worshipped alongside Him others among the intermediaries whom they thought would benefit them or bring them near to Allah in closeness.

The messengers said to them: ﴿He invites you, that He may forgive you of your sins﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, ﴿and defer you to a specified term﴾, that is, in this world, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And that you should seek forgiveness from your Lord, then repent to Him, He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term and give every doer of virtue his virtue﴾ [Hud: 3]. Then the peoples said to them, disputing in the position of prophethood, after assuming their concession of the first position, and the summary of what they said: ﴿You are only human beings like us﴾, meaning: How shall we follow you merely on your word, when we have not seen from you a miracle? ﴿So bring us a clear authority﴾, meaning: a supernatural sign that we propose to you.

Their messengers said to them: ﴿We are only human beings like you﴾, meaning: It is true that I am a human being like you in humanity, ﴿but Allah bestows His favour upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, meaning: with messengership and prophethood. ﴿And it was not for us to bring you an authority﴾ according to what you asked ﴿except by the permission of Allah﴾, meaning: after we ask Him and He permits us in that. ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾, meaning: in all their affairs.

Then the messengers said: ﴿And why should we not rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: what prevents us from relying upon Him, when He has guided us to the most upright, clearest and most evident paths? ﴿And we will surely bear patiently what you have caused us harm﴾, meaning: of evil speech and foolish deeds. ﴿And upon Allah let those who rely [upon Him] rely.﴾

He, may He be exalted, informs of what the disbelieving nations threatened their messengers with: expulsion from their land and banishment from among them. Thus the people of Shu'ayb said to him and to those who believed with him: ﴿O Shu'ayb, we will surely expel you and those who believed with you from our town, or you will return to our religion﴾ [Al-A'raf: 88]. The people of Lot said: ﴿Expel the family of Lot from your town. Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure﴾ [An-Naml: 56]. And He, may He be exalted, said, informing about the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿And indeed, they almost induced you to slip from the land to expel you from it; and then they would not remain after you, except for a little﴾ [Al-Isra': 76]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And [recall] when those who disbelieved plotted against you, to confine you, or kill you, or expel you. They plot, and Allah plots. And Allah is the best of planners﴾ [Al-Anfal: 30].

Among the works of Allah, may He be exalted, was that He made His Messenger prevail and gave him victory. Because of his departure from Makkah, He made for him helpers, supporters and an army who fight in the way of Allah. He continued to elevate him, may Allah the Exalted, from one stage to another, until He granted him the conquest of Makkah, the city that had expelled him, and established him there, and humbled the noses of his enemies from among them and from all the people of the earth. People entered the religion of Allah in multitudes, and the word of Allah and His religion became dominant over all other religions, in the eastern and western parts of the earth, in the shortest time. For this reason He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Then their Lord revealed to them, "We will surely destroy the wrongdoers, and We will surely settle you in the land after them"﴾. As He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿And Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers, that they would surely be helped, and that Our soldiers would surely be the victorious﴾ [As-Saffat: 171–173]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Allah has decreed, "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [Al-Mujadilah: 21]. And He said: ﴿And We have already written in the Zabur, after the reminder, that the earth will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾ [Al-Anbiya': 105]. ﴿Moses said to his people, "Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 128]. And He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern and western parts of the land which We had blessed. And the good word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of their patience, and We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had been constructing and what they had been erecting﴾ [Al-A'raf: 137].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿That is for one who fears My standing [before Me] and fears My threat﴾. That is: this threat of Mine is for one who fears standing before Me on the Day of Resurrection and fears My threat, which is My warning and My punishment. As He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿But as for one who transgressed and preferred the worldly life, indeed, Hellfire will be his refuge. And as for one who feared the standing [before] his Lord and restrained the soul from [its] desire, indeed, Paradise will be [his] refuge﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 37–41]. And He said: ﴿And for one who fears the standing before his Lord are two gardens﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 46].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they sought victory﴾, that is: the messengers sought help from their Lord against their peoples. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and Qatadah.

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: the nations sought victory against themselves, as they said: ﴿O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾ [Al-Anfal: 32].

It is possible that both meanings are intended, just as they sought victory against themselves on the day of Badr, and the Messenger of Allah sought victory and help. Allah, may He be exalted, said to the polytheists: ﴿If you seek a decision, the decision has certainly come to you. And if you cease, it is better for you﴾, etc. [Al-Anfal: 19]. And Allah knows best.

﴿And every obstinate tyrant was disappointed﴾. That is: one who is domineering within himself, opposing the truth, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Throw into Hell every obstinate disbeliever, a hinderer of good, a transgressor, a doubter, who set up with Allah another deity; so throw him into the severe punishment﴾ [Qaf: 24–26].

And in a hadith: "Indeed, Hell will be brought on the Day of Resurrection, and it will call out to the creation, saying: 'I have been entrusted with every obstinate tyrant...'" to the end of the hadith [[Narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (3/40) from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him. It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. (2574), by way of al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan, gharib, sahih hadith."]].

He was disappointed and lost when the prophets exerted themselves in supplication to their Lord, the Mighty, the Omnipotent.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Behind him is Hell﴾. Here "behind" (waraa') means "in front of" (amam), as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And there was behind them a king who seized every ship by force﴾ [Al-Kahf: 79]. Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it as: "And there was in front of them a king."

That is: behind the obstinate tyrant is Hell; that is, it lies in wait for him, he will abide in it forever on the Day of Return, and it will be presented to him morning and evening until the Day of Calling Out.

﴿And he will be given to drink of pus﴾. That is: in the Fire he has no drink except from boiling water or ghassaq. This one is in extreme heat, and that one is in extreme cold and stench, as He said: ﴿This—so let them taste it: boiling water and ghassaq, and other [torments] of its kind in pairs﴾ [Sad: 57–58].

Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: al-sadid is of pus and blood.

Qatadah said: it is what flows from his flesh and skin. And in another report from him: al-sadid is what comes out of the inside of the disbeliever, mixed with pus and blood.

From the hadith of Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid ibn al-Sakan, she said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the clay of al-khabal?" He said: "The pus of the people of the Fire." [[Narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (6/460).]] And in another narration: "The essence of the people of the Fire." [[This is the narration of Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (5/171).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ali ibn Ishaq narrated to us, 'Abdullah informed us, Safwan ibn 'Amr informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Bisr, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying: ﴿and he will be given to drink of pus, which he will gulp down﴾. He said: "It is brought near to him, and he dislikes it. When it is brought close to him, it scorches his face, and the skin of his scalp falls off. When he drinks it, it cuts his intestines until it comes out from his anus. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And they will be given boiling water, which will cut their intestines﴾ [Muhammad: 15], and He says: ﴿And if they call for relief, they will be relieved with water like molten metal, which scorches the faces. Wretched is the drink﴾ [Al-Kahf: 29]."[[Al-Musnad (5/265).]]

Thus it was narrated by Ibn Jarir, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with it [[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/549). It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, no. (2583), by way of 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak with it, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith. Likewise Muhammad ibn Isma'il said it from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Bisr, and we do not know 'Ubayd Allah ibn Bisr except in this hadith."]]. He and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid, from Safwan ibn 'Amr, with it [[Al-Tabari narrated it in his tafsir (16/551) by way of Hayawah ibn Shurayh from Baqiyyah, with it.]].

As for His saying: ﴿yatajarra'uhu﴾, that is: he swallows it with difficulty and dislike, that is, he drinks it by force and compulsion, not putting it in his mouth until the angel strikes him with an iron mace, as He said: ﴿And for them are maces of iron﴾ [Al-Hajj: 21].

﴿And he almost cannot swallow it﴾. That is: he chokes on it because of its evil color, taste and smell, and its heat or cold, which is unbearable.

﴿And death will come to him from every place﴾. That is: all his body, limbs and members will be in pain.

Maymun ibn Mihran said: from every bone, vein and sinew.

'Ikrimah said: even from the ends of his hair.

Ibrahim al-Taymi said: from the place of every hair, that is, from his body, even from the ends of his hair.

Ibn Jarir said: ﴿And death will come to him from every place﴾ means: from in front of him and behind him, from his right and left, from above him, from beneath his feet, and from all the rest of his body's parts.

Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And death will come to him from every place﴾, he said: the kinds of punishment with which Allah will punish him on the Day of Resurrection in the Fire of Hell. There is no kind of it except that death comes to him from it—if he were to die, but he does not die, because Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿It will not be decreed for them so that they might die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾ [Fatir: 36].

The meaning of the words of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, is that there is no kind of these punishments except that when it strikes him, it necessitates that he die from it, if he were to die; but he does not die, so that he may remain eternally in the continuance of punishment and torment. For this reason He said: ﴿And death will come to him from every place, yet he will not die﴾.

Among the works of Allah, may He be exalted, was that He made His Messenger prevail and gave him victory. This is a parable which Allah, exalted is He, struck for the deeds of the disbelievers who worshipped other than Allah alongside Him, denied His messengers, and built their deeds on no sound foundation. So they collapsed, and they lost them when they needed them most. Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord: their deeds are like ashes﴾, meaning: the example of the deeds of those who disbelieved on the Day of Resurrection, when they seek their reward from Allah, exalted is He, because they used to think that they were upon something, but they find nothing, and they find nothing gathered except what gathers from ashes when a fierce wind blows hard upon it, ﴿on a stormy day﴾, meaning: a day of strong, violent wind. So they are unable to retain anything of their deeds which they earned in the worldly life [[Addition from manuscripts T and A.]], just as they are unable to gather this ash on this day. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: The people of the Fire said to one another, "Come, for the people of Paradise attained Paradise only through their weeping and their humbling themselves before Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Come, let us weep and humble ourselves before Allah." So they wept and humbled themselves. When they saw that this did not benefit them, they said, "Come, for the people of Paradise attained Paradise only through patience. Come, let us be patient." So they were patient with a patience the like of which had never been seen, but that did not benefit them. At that they said: ﴿It is all the same for us whether we show distress or we are patient; there is for us no place of escape﴾

I say: Apparently this mutual argument takes place in the Fire after they have entered it, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when they dispute within the Fire, the weak will say to those who were arrogant, "Indeed we were following you, so will you relieve us of a portion of the Fire?" Those who were arrogant will say, "Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, Allah has judged between the servants."﴾ [Ghafir: 47, 48]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿[Allah] will say, "Enter among nations that have passed on before you of jinn and mankind into the Fire." Every time a nation enters, it curses its sister until, when they have all overtaken one another therein, the last of them will say about the first of them, "Our Lord, these had led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He will say, "For each is double, but you do not know." And the first of them will say to the last of them, "You had no favor over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn."﴾ [Al-A'raf: 38, 39]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿On the Day their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger." And they will say, "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our great ones, and they led us astray from the way." "Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse."﴾ [Al-Ahzab: 66-68].

As for their disputing at the gathering place (al-Mahshar), Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning speech to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Were it not for you, we would have been believers." Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals." And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and attribute to Him equals." And they will conceal regret when they see the punishment. And We will put shackles upon the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ [Saba': 31-33].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of what Iblis (may Allah curse him) addressed to his followers after Allah had judged between His servants, admitting the believers into the Gardens and settling the disbelievers in the lowest depths. At that time Iblis, may Allah curse him, stood among them as a speaker, in order to increase their sorrow over their sorrow, their loss over their loss, and their regret over their regret. He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth﴾, meaning: through the tongues of His messengers, and He promised you that in following them there would be salvation and safety. That was a true promise and a truthful report. As for me, I promised you and then broke my promise to you, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He promises them and arouses their desires, but Satan promises them nothing except delusion﴾ [An-Nisa: 120].

Then he said: ﴿And I had no authority over you﴾, meaning: I had no proof or argument in what I called you to, nor any evidence for the truth of what I promised you. ﴿But I called you, and you responded to me﴾ merely by that. Yet the messengers had established against you the proofs and the sound evidences for the truth of what they brought you, but you opposed them and so you came to what you are in. ﴿So do not blame me﴾ today, ﴿but blame yourselves﴾, for the sin is yours, because you opposed the proofs and followed me merely because I called you to falsehood. ﴿I cannot help you﴾, meaning: I cannot benefit you, rescue you, or deliver you from what you are in, ﴿nor can you help me﴾, meaning: you cannot benefit me by rescuing me from what I am in of punishment and torment. ﴿Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me [with Allah] before﴾.

Qatadah said: meaning, "because of your associating me before."

Ibn Jarir said: he means, "I denied that I was a partner to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

And this which he said is the more apparent (rajih), as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5-6], and He said: ﴿No! They will deny their worship of them and will be opposed to them﴾ [Maryam: 82].

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers﴾, meaning: in their turning away from the truth and their following of falsehood, ﴿will have a painful punishment﴾.

The apparent meaning from the context of the verse is that this address is from Iblis after they have entered the Fire, as we have already mentioned. However, a hadith has been narrated, which Ibn Abi Hatim related, and this is his wording, and Ibn Jarir (related) through the narration of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad: "Dukhayn al-Hajri narrated to me, from Uqbah ibn Amir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: 'When Allah gathers the first and the last, and judges between them, and finishes the judgment, the believers will say: "Our Lord has judged between us, so who will intercede for us?" They will say: "Let us go to Adam" — and he mentioned Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, and Isa — and Isa will say: "I will direct you to the unlettered Prophet." So they will come to me, and Allah will permit me to rise to Him, and I will rise from my gathering with the finest fragrance anyone has ever smelled, until I come to my Lord, and He will grant me intercession and will give me light from the hair of my head to the nail of my foot. He will rise from his gathering with the foulest smell anyone has ever smelled, and then their wailing will intensify.'" ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided: Indeed, Allah promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I broke it with you. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they will be met therein with greeting and peace﴾ [Al-Furqan: 75]. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 14, verses 24–26:

Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words ﴿a parable: a good word﴾: it is the testimony that there is no god but Allah. ﴿Like a good tree﴾: it is the believer. ﴿Its root is firmly fixed﴾: he means that "There is no god but Allah" is firmly fixed in the heart of the believer. ﴿And its branches are in the sky﴾: he means that the deed of the believer is raised by it up to the sky.

Likewise said ad-Dahhak, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ikrimah, Qatadah and others besides them: this is an expression for the believer, his good word, and his righteous deed. The believer is like the palm tree, for a righteous deed is continually raised up for him at every time and moment, morning and evening.

As-Suddi narrated the same from Murrah, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "It is the palm tree."

Shu'bah narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas: "It is the palm tree."

Hammad ibn Salamah narrated from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a platter of unripe dates (busr), and he recited: "And the parable of a good word is like a good tree," and said: "It is the palm tree." [Narrated by at-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/570) and at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan, no. 3119, by way of Hammad ibn Salamah. at-Tirmidhi said: "Others have narrated the like of this as a mawquf (halted) report, and we know of no one who raised it (to the Prophet) except Hammad ibn Salamah. Ma'mar, Hammad ibn Zayd and others narrated it without raising it."]

It is also narrated from this route and others, from Anas, as a mawquf report [narrated by Abu Bakr ibn Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from his father, from Anas ibn Malik, similar, as a mawquf report, recorded by at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan, no. 3119; and Hammad ibn Zayd narrated from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas, as a mawquf report, recorded by at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan, no. 3119]. Likewise Masruq, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, ad-Dahhak, Qatadah and others explicitly stated it.

al-Bukhari said: Ubayd ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Abu Usamah, from Ubaydullah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: 'Tell me about a tree that resembles, or is like, the Muslim man. Its leaves do not fall, and it yields its fruit at every time.'" Ibn 'Umar said: "It occurred to my mind that it was the palm tree. But I saw Abu Bakr and 'Umar not speaking, so I disliked to speak. When they said nothing, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'It is the palm tree.'" When we rose, I said to 'Umar: "O father! By Allah, it had occurred to my mind that it was the palm tree." He said: "What prevented you from speaking?" He said: "I did not see you speaking, so I disliked to speak or to say anything." 'Umar said: "For you to have said it would be dearer to me than such-and-such." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4698.]

Ahmad said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "I accompanied Ibn 'Umar to Madinah, and I did not hear him narrate from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except one hadith." He said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he was brought some fruit-stalks (jimar, i.e., palm fruit clusters). He said: 'Among the trees there is a tree whose likeness is that of the Muslim man.' I wanted to say: 'It is the palm tree,' but I looked and found that I was the youngest of the people, so I kept silent. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'It is the palm tree.'" [Musnad Ahmad (2/12); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 72; Sahih Muslim, no. 2811.]

Malik and 'Abd al-'Aziz narrated, from 'Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day to his companions: "Among the trees there is a tree whose leaf does not fall, like the believer." He said: "The people then began naming the trees of the desert, and it came into my heart that it was the palm tree. [So I was shy, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'It is the palm tree.']" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 131; Sahih Muslim, no. 2811.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Aban (i.e., Ibn Yazid al-'Attar) narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us: that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, the people of wealth have taken away the rewards!" He said: "Do you see, if someone were to gather the goods of this world and stack some of them upon others, would it reach the sky? Shall I not tell you of a deed whose root is in the earth and whose branch is in the sky?" He said: "What is it, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "You say: 'There is no god but Allah, Allah is greatest, Glory be to Allah, and Praise be to Allah,' ten times after every prayer. That is its root in the earth and its branch in the sky." [Cited by as-Suyuti in ad-Durr al-Manthur (5/22), attributing it to Ibn Abi Hatim; it is mursal.]

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning ﴿like a good tree﴾ that he said: "It is a tree in Paradise."

* *

As for His words ﴿yielding its fruit at every time﴾, it was said: morning and evening. It was said: every month. It was said: every two months. It was said: every six months. It was said: every seven months. It was said: every year.

The apparent meaning from the context is that the believer's likeness is that of a tree from which fruit is always found at every time, whether in summer or winter, by night or by day. Likewise, the believer always has a righteous deed raised up for him during the hours of the night and the ends of the day, at every time and moment.

﴿By the permission of its Lord﴾: that is, complete, good, abundant and pure. ﴿And Allah sets forth parables for the people that they may remember.﴾

* *

As for His words ﴿And the parable of an evil word is like an evil tree﴾: this is the parable of the disbelief of the disbeliever, which has no root and no stability. It is likened to the tree of al-Hanzal (colocynth), which is called ash-Shiryan. [Shu'bah narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas ibn Malik: that it is the colocynth tree.]

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar, the hafiz, said: Yahya ibn Muhammad ibn as-Sakan narrated to us, Abu Zayd Sa'id ibn ar-Rabi' narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Anas, who I think raised it (to the Prophet), who said: "'And the parable of a good word is like a good tree,' he said: 'It is the palm tree.' '﻿And the parable of an evil word is like an evil tree,' he said: 'It is ash-Shiryan.'" [Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas, raised to the Prophet, similarly; narrated by at-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/570, 585).]

Then he narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Mu'awiyah, from Anas, as a mawquf report. [Narrated by at-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/583) from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna as a mawquf report; Shababah and 'Amr ibn al-Haytham also narrated from Shu'bah and halted it. See Tafsir at-Tabari (16/583).]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Hammad, that is Ibn Salamah, narrated to us, from Shu'ayb ibn al-Habhab, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "'And the parable of an evil word is like an evil tree,' it is the colocynth (al-Hanzalah)." I informed Abu al-'Aliyah of this, and he said: "Thus we used to hear."

Ibn Jarir also narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah, with the same chain. [Tafsir at-Tabari (16/585).] Abu Ya'la narrated it in his Musnad in more detail, saying: Ghassan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Anas: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was brought a platter with unripe dates on it, and he said: "And the parable of a good word is like a good tree, its root is firmly fixed and its branches are in the sky, yielding its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord." Then he said: "It is the palm tree." "And the parable of an evil word is like an evil tree, uprooted from the surface of the earth, having no stability," he said: "It is the colocynth (al-Hanzal)." Shu'ayb said: "I informed Abu al-'Aliyah of this, and he said: 'Thus we used to hear.'" [Also narrated by at-Tirmidhi in as-Sunan, no. 3119, from 'Abd ibn Humayd, from Abu al-Walid, from Hammad ibn Salamah, similarly; the discussion of it has already passed.]

* *
