Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 14, verse 27 (part 1 of 5):

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Alqamah ibn Marthad informed me, he said: I heard Sa'd ibn 'Ubaydah, on the authority of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may God be pleased with him), that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When a Muslim is questioned in the grave, he testifies that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. That is His saying: ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾" [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4699.]].

It was also related by Muslim and by all the rest of the compilers, from the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same wording [[Sahih Muslim, no. 2871; Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4750; Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3120; Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/101); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4269.]].

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, on the authority of al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib, who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) for the funeral of a man from the Ansar. We reached the grave, and it had not yet been dug into its niche (lahd). The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat down and we sat around him, as if birds were perched upon our heads. In his hand was a stick with which he was scratching the ground. He raised his head and said: "Seek refuge with God from the punishment of the grave," twice or three times. Then he said: "When the believing servant is at the point of departing from this world and turning towards the Hereafter, angels come down to him from heaven, with bright faces as if their faces were the sun, carrying a shroud from the shrouds of Paradise and perfume from the perfumes of Paradise. They sit at a distance from him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes until he sits at his head and says: 'O good soul, come forth to forgiveness from God and good pleasure.'"

He said: "So it comes out flowing like a drop flows from the mouth of a water-skin. He takes it, and when he has taken it, they do not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye. They take it and place it in that shroud and in that perfume, and there issues from it the most fragrant scent of musk ever found upon the face of the earth. They ascend with it, and they do not pass with it by any assembly of angels without them saying: 'What is this good spirit?' They say: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so,' using the best of the names by which he was called in the world, until they reach the lowest heaven and ask for it to be opened, and it is opened for him. Those nearest to God in each heaven escort him to the next heaven, until he reaches the seventh heaven. Then God says: 'Record the book of My servant in 'Illiyyin, and return him to the earth, for from it I created them, into it I shall return them, and from it I shall bring them out once more.'"

He said: "His spirit is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him, and they say to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is God.' They say: 'What is your religion?' He says: 'My religion is Islam.' They say: 'What is this man who was sent among you?' He says: 'He is the Messenger of God.' They say: 'And what is your knowledge?' He says: 'I read the Book of God, I believed in it and I affirmed it.' Then a caller calls from heaven: 'My servant has spoken the truth. Spread for him from Paradise, clothe him from Paradise, and open for him a door to Paradise.'" He said: "So its breeze and fragrance come to him, and his grave is widened for him as far as his eye can see. A man of fine face, fine clothes and pleasant scent comes to him and says: 'Rejoice in that which will delight you. This is your day which you were promised.' He says to him: 'Who are you? Your face is a face that brings good.' He says: 'I am your righteous deed.' He says: 'My Lord, establish the Hour, my Lord, establish the Hour, so that I may return to my family and my property.'"

He said: "As for the disbelieving servant, when he is at the point of departing from this world and turning towards the Hereafter, angels with black faces come down to him from heaven, carrying coarse garments (masuh), and they sit at a distance from him as far as the eye can see. Then the Angel of Death comes until he sits at his head and says: 'O evil soul, come forth to the wrath and anger of God.'" He said: "So it scatters through his body, and he pulls it out as a skewer is pulled out of wet wool. He takes it, and when he has taken it, they do not leave it in his hand for the blink of an eye, until they place it in those coarse garments. There issues from it the foulest stench of a carcass ever found upon the face of the earth. They ascend with it, and they do not pass with it by any assembly of angels without them saying: 'What is this evil spirit?' They say: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so,' using the worst of the names by which he was called in the world, until he reaches the lowest heaven, and it is requested to be opened for him, but it is not opened for him."

Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) recited: ﴿The gates of heaven will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until the camel passes through the eye of the needle﴾ [al-A'raf: 40]. "God says: 'Record his book in Sijjin, in the lowest earth,' and his spirit is cast down, casting." Then he recited: ﴿And whoever associates others with God, it is as if he had fallen from the sky and the birds snatched him, or the wind threw him into a faraway place﴾ [al-Hajj: 31].

"His spirit is returned to his body, and two angels come to him and seat him and say to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'Hah hah, I do not know.' They say to him: 'What is your religion?' He says: 'Hah hah, I do not know.' They say to him: 'What is this man who was sent among you?' He says: 'Hah hah, I do not know.' Then a caller calls from heaven: 'He has lied. Spread for him from the Fire and open for him a door to the Fire.' So its heat and scorching winds come to him, and his grave is constricted upon him until his ribs interlock. A man of ugly face, ugly clothes and foul smell comes to him and says: 'Rejoice in that which will grieve you. This is your day which you were promised.' He says: 'Who are you? Your face is a face that brings evil.' He says: 'I am your evil deed.' He says: 'My Lord, do not establish the Hour.'"

Abu Dawud related it from the hadith of al-A'mash, and al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, with the same wording [[Al-Musnad (4/287); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 4753; Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/78); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 1548.]].

Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, on the authority of Yunus ibn Khabbab [[In MS h and a: "Yunus ibn Habib"; the reading in the text is from MS t and the Musnad.]], on the authority of al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, on the authority of Zadhan, on the authority of al-Bara' ibn 'Azib (may God be pleased with him), who said: We went out with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to a funeral, and he mentioned something similar.

In it: "When his spirit departs, every angel between heaven and earth prays over him, and every angel in heaven, and the gates of heaven are opened. There is no one at any gate except that they are supplicating God, Mighty and Majestic, that He raise his spirit up through them."

At its end: "Then there is assigned to him a blind, deaf and mute one, who has in his hand a mace, which if a mountain were struck with it, it would become dust. He strikes him one blow and he becomes dust. Then God, Mighty and Majestic, restores him as he was, and he strikes him another blow, and he cries out a cry which everything hears except the two worlds (al-thaqalan: humans and jinn)." Al-Bara' said: "Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and he is spread with the bedding of the Fire" [[Al-Musnad (4/295).]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Khaythamah, on the authority of al-Bara' regarding the words of the Exalted: ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world﴾, that it is: the punishment of the grave.

Al-Mas'udi said, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mukhariq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud): "When the believer dies, he is seated in his grave, and it is said to him: 'Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your prophet?' God makes him firm, and he says: 'My Lord is God, my religion is Islam, and my prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ).'" 'Abd Allah recited: ﴿God makes firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [[Related by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/597).]].

Imam 'Abd ibn Humayd, may God have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shayban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, who said: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When the servant is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, he indeed hears the sound of their sandals." He said: "Then two angels come to him and seat him, and they say to him: 'What did you used to say about this man?'" He said: "As for the believer, he says: 'I bear witness that he is the servant of God and His Messenger.'" He said: "It is said to him: 'Look at your seat in the Fire; God has replaced it for you with a seat in Paradise.'" The Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "So he sees both of them." Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that his grave is widened for him to seventy cubits, and it is filled with green (plants) until the Day of Resurrection."

Muslim related it on the authority of 'Abd ibn Humayd, with the same wording [[Al-Muntakhab li-'Abd ibn Humayd, no. 1178; Sahih Muslim, no. 2870.]]. Al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, with the same wording [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (4/97).]].

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he asked Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah about the two questioners of the grave (fattanai al-qabr), and he said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'This community will be tested in its graves. When the believer is placed in his grave and his companions turn away from him, there comes an angel of severe reproach, who says to him: What did you used to say about this man? The believer says: I say that he is the Messenger of God and His servant. The angel says to him: Look at your seat in the Fire, which God has saved you from, and He has replaced for you your seat in the Fire with your seat in Paradise, which you see.' So he sees both of them. The believer says: 'Let me give glad tidings to my family.' It is said to him: 'Be still.'" "As for the hypocrite, when his family turns away from him, he is seated and it is said to him: 'What did you used to say about this man?' He says: 'I do not know; I used to say what people say.' It is said to him: 'You did not know! This is your seat in Paradise which was yours, but it has been replaced for you with your seat in the Fire.'"

Jabir said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Every servant will be raised in his grave according to how he died: the believer upon his faith, and the hypocrite upon his hypocrisy."

Its chain of narration is sound according to the condition of Muslim, but the two (Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it [[In the Musnad (3/346): "Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, on the authority of Abu al-Zubayr with it," and similarly in Ibn Hajar's Atraf al-Musnad (2/110).]].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 14, verse 27 (part 2 of 5):

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, 'Abbad ibn Rashid narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: "We witnessed a funeral with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O people, this Ummah will be tested in its graves. When a person is buried and his companions turn away from him, an angel comes to him holding a hammer, and he makes him sit up and says: What do you say about this man? If he is a believer, he says: I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the servant of Allah and His Messenger. [Footnote: In A: "And that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."] Then it is said to him: You have spoken the truth. Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said: This was your abode had you disbelieved in your Lord. But since you believed, this is your abode. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and he wishes to rise towards it, but it is said to him: Be still. And his grave is widened for him.' And if he is a disbeliever or a hypocrite, it is said to him [Footnote: In T and A: "Then it is said."]: What do you say about this man? He says: I do not know. I heard the people saying something, so I said it. It is said to him: You neither knew nor followed, nor were you guided. Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: This was your abode had you believed in your Lord. But since you disbelieved in Him, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has replaced it for you with this. Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and he is struck with a blow of the hammer that is heard by all of Allah's creation, Mighty and Majestic, except the two worlds (jinn and humankind).'" Some of the people said: "O Messenger of Allah, no one upon whom an angel stands holding a hammer is left without being terrified at that moment." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then recited: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word﴾. [Footnote: Al-Musnad (3/3).]

This is also a chain of narration with no harm in it, for 'Abbad ibn Rashid al-Tamimi was narrated from by al-Bukhari in a conjoined narration, but some have criticised him.

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr ibn 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Yasar, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [Footnote: In T and A: "From the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said."] that he said: "Indeed, when the deceased is attended by the angels, if he is a righteous man they say: Come forth, O soul that was at peace [Footnote: In T and A: "the good soul"], that was in a good body. Come forth praiseworthy, and rejoice in rest, sweet fragrance, and a Lord who is not angry." He said: "Such words continue to be said to it until it departs. Then it is raised up to the heaven, and permission is sought for it to enter, and it is asked: Who is this? It is said: So-and-so. They say: Welcome to the good soul that was in a good body. Enter, praiseworthy, and rejoice in rest, sweet fragrance, and a Lord who is not angry." He said: "Such words continue to be said to it until it reaches the heaven in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is."

"And if the man is evil, they say: Come forth, O evil soul that was in an evil body. Come forth blameworthy, and rejoice in boiling water, and pus, and other punishments of their kind. Such words continue to be said to it until it departs. Then it is raised up to the heaven, and permission is sought for it to enter, and it is asked: Who is this? It is said: So-and-so. It is said: There is no welcome for the evil soul that was in an evil body. Return blameworthy, for the doors of the heaven will not be opened for you. Then it is sent down from the heaven, and it returns to the grave." So the righteous man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith, and the evil man sits up and is asked the same as was mentioned in the first hadith.

Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated it through the route of Ibn Abi Dhi'b with similar wording. [Footnote: Al-Musnad (2/364); Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4262); al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (3/311): "This is a sound chain, and its narrators are trustworthy."]

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "When the soul of the believing servant departs, two angels meet it and ascend with it." Hammad said: "He mentioned the goodness of its fragrance and mentioned musk." He said: "And the people of the heaven say: A good soul has come from the direction of the earth. May Allah bless you and the body you used to inhabit. It is then taken to its Lord, Mighty and Majestic, and He says: Take it to the furthest term." "And when the soul of the disbeliever departs." Hammad said: "He mentioned its stench and mentioned curse." "And the people of the heaven say: An evil soul has come from the direction of the earth." He said: "It is said: Take it to the furthest term." Abu Hurayrah said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then lowered a cloth that was over his nose, like this." [Footnote: Sahih Muslim, no. (2872).]

Ibn Hibban said in his Sahih: Umar ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani narrated to us, Zayd ibn Akhzam narrated to us, Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, my father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Qasamah ibn Zuhayr, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Indeed, when the believer is taken, the angels of mercy come to him with a white silk cloth, and they say: Come forth to the comfort of Allah. So it comes out like the most fragrant musk, to the extent that they pass it to one another, smelling it, until they bring it to the gate of the heaven. They say: What is this good fragrance that has come from the direction of the earth? And they do not come to any heaven without saying the same thing, until they bring it to the spirits of the believers. They are happier with it than the people of an absent one are with their absent relative. They ask: What has so-and-so done? They reply: Leave him until he rests, for he was in distress! Then he says: He has died. Did he not come to you? They say: He has been taken to his mother, the Abyss (al-Hawiyah). As for the disbeliever, the angels of punishment come to him with a rough cloth and say: Come forth to the wrath of Allah. So it comes out like the most foul stench of a carcass, and it is taken to the gate of the earth." [Footnote: Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (733), Mawarid edition.]

It has also been narrated through the route of Hammam ibn Yahya, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Jawza', from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), with similar wording. He said: "It is asked: What has so-and-so done? What has so-and-so done? What has such-and-such a woman done?" He said: "As for the disbeliever, when his soul is taken and he is brought to the gate of the earth, the keepers of the earth say: We have never found a stench more foul than this. Then it is taken down to the lowest earth." [Footnote: Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (731), Mawarid edition; al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (1/351) through the route of Hammam with similar wording, and al-Hakim declared it sound and al-Dhahabi agreed.]

Qatadah said: "A man narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The spirits of the believers are gathered at al-Jabiyah, and the spirits of the disbelievers are gathered at Barhut, a salt flat in Hadramawt."

Al-Hafiz Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Yahya ibn Khalaf narrated to us, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the deceased, or one of you, is buried, two black-blue angels come to him. One of them is called al-Munkar and the other al-Nakir. They say: What did you used to say about this man? He says what he used to say: He is the servant of Allah and His Messenger; I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. They say: We knew that you would say this. Then his grave is widened for him, seventy cubits by seventy. Then it is illuminated for him, and it is said to him: Sleep. He says: Let me return to my family and inform them. They say: Sleep the sleep of the bridegroom, whom none wakes except the dearest of his family to him, until Allah raises him from that resting place. And if he was a hypocrite, he says: I heard the people saying something, so I said the same as them. I do not know. They say: We knew that you would say that. Then it is said to the earth: Close in upon him. It closes in upon him, and his ribs interlock, and he remains there being punished until Allah raises him from that resting place." [Footnote: Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (1071).]

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan gharib hadith.

Hammad ibn Salamah said, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, reciting: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. He said: "That is when it is asked of him in the grave: Who is your Lord, and what is your religion? He says: My Lord is Allah, my religion is Islam, and my Prophet is Muhammad, who brought us the clear proofs from Allah, so I believed in him and affirmed him. It is said to him: You have spoken the truth. Upon this you lived, upon this you died, and upon this you will be raised." [Footnote: Narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (16/596).]

Ibn Jarir said: Mujahid ibn Musa and al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, and they both said: Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Amr informed us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah: "Indeed the deceased hears the sound of their sandals when they turn away from him, retreating. If he was a believer, prayer is at his head, zakat is at his right, fasting is at his left, and good deeds such as charity, kinship ties, kindness, and benevolence to people are at his feet. He is approached from the direction of his head, and prayer says: There is no entrance from my side. He is approached from his right, and zakat says: There is no entrance from my side. He is approached from his left, and fasting says: There is no entrance from my side. He is approached from his feet, and the good deeds say: There is no entrance from my side. Then it is said to him: Sit up."

"So he sits up, and the sun has been shaped for him, having drawn near to setting. It is said to him: Tell us about what we ask you. He says: Leave me until I pray. It is said: You will do so, but tell us about what we ask you. He says: What do you ask me about? It is said: Tell us about this man who was among you: what do you say about him, and what do you testify concerning him? He says: Muhammad? It is said to him: Yes. He says: I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah, and that he came to us with the clear proofs from Allah, so we affirmed him. It is said to him: Upon this you lived, upon this you died, and upon this you will be raised, if Allah wills. Then his grave is widened for him seventy cubits, and it is illuminated for him, and a door to Paradise is opened for him. It is said to him: Look at what Allah has prepared for you in it. So he increases in joy and happiness. Then his soul is placed among the good breath, and they are green birds that hang from the trees of Paradise. And the body is returned to that from which it was originated, which is dust." And that is the saying of Allah: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. [Footnote: Tafsir al-Tabari (16/596, 597).]

Ibn Hibban narrated it through the route of al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn 'Amr, and he mentioned the answer of the disbeliever and his punishment. [Footnote: Sahih Ibn Hibban, no. (781), Mawarid edition.]

Al-Bazzar said: Sa'id ibn Bahr al-Qaratisi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn al-Qasim narrated to us, Yazid ibn Kaysan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, who said, I think he traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ): "When death comes upon the believer and he witnesses what he witnesses, he wishes that his soul would leave [[In T: "fawadda".]] (meaning his soul), while Allah loves to meet him. The believer's soul is raised to the heaven, and the souls of the believers come to him and ask him about their acquaintances among the people of the earth. When he says, 'I left so-and-so on earth [[In A: "in the world".]],' they are pleased by that. When he says, 'So-and-so has died,' they say, 'He has not been brought to us.' The believer sits in his grave and is asked: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah' [[In T: "Allah is my Lord".]]. He is asked: 'Who is your Prophet?' He says: 'Muhammad is my Prophet' [[In T and A: "my Prophet Muhammad".]]. He is asked: 'What is your religion?' He says: 'My religion is Islam.' A door is opened for him in his grave, and it is said to him (or he says): 'Look at your seat.' Then he sees the grave as if it had been a moment of sleep. As for the enemy of Allah, when death comes upon him and he witnesses what he witnesses, he never wishes his soul to leave, while Allah hates to meet him. When he sits in his grave (or is made to sit), he is asked: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'I do not know.' It is said to him: 'You do not know.' A door of Hell is opened for him, and he is struck with a blow that every creature hears except the two weighty ones [[Jinn and humans.]]. Then it is said to him: 'Sleep as the one bitten sleeps.'" I said to Abu Hurayrah: "What is the one bitten?" He said: "The one whom the creatures and snakes bite, and then his grave is narrowed upon him."

Then he said: We do not know of this being narrated except by al-Walid ibn al-Qasim. [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (874), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in Majma' (3/52): "Part of it is in the Sahih. Al-Bazzar narrated it, and its narrators are trustworthy except Sa'id ibn Bahr al-Qaratisi, whom I do not know."]]

Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Hujayn ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Salamah al-Majishun narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: Asma', the daughter of al-Siddiq (meaning Asma' bint Abi Bakr), may Allah be pleased with her, used to narrate from the Prophet (ﷺ). She said: He said: "When a person enters his grave, if he is a believer, his deeds surround him: the prayer and the fasting." He said: "The angel comes to him from the direction of the prayer, and the prayer repels him; and from the direction of the fasting, and the fasting repels him." He said: "Then he calls to him: 'Sit!' So he sits. He says to him: 'What do you say about this man?' meaning the Prophet (ﷺ). He says: 'Who?' He says: 'Muhammad.' He says: 'I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah.' He says: 'What would make you know? Did you meet him?' He says: 'I bear witness that he is the Messenger of Allah.' He says: 'Upon that you lived, upon it you died, and upon it you will be resurrected.' And if he was a wicked person or a disbeliever, the angel comes to him with nothing between him and it [[In T: "He said: And if."]] to repel him. He makes him sit and says: 'Sit! What do you say about this man?' He says: 'Which man?' He says: 'Muhammad?' He says: 'By Allah, I do not know. I heard people say something, so I said it.' The angel says to him: 'Upon that you lived, upon it you died, and upon it you will be resurrected.' He said: 'And a creature is let loose upon him in his grave, with a whip whose stroke is a burning coal like the bottom of a camel's [[In T and A: "Mar-ghar"?]] ... it strikes him as Allah wills, deaf, it does not hear his voice, so it has no mercy on him.'" [[Musnad (6/352).]]

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, regarding this verse: "When death is present to the believer, the angels witness it, greet him and give him the good news of Paradise. When he dies, they walk with his funeral, and then they pray over him along with the people. When he is buried, he is made to sit in his grave, and it is said to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'My Lord is Allah.' It is said to him: 'Who is your Messenger?' He says: 'Muhammad (ﷺ).' It is said to him: 'What is your testimony?' He says: 'I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.' His grave is widened for him as far as his sight reaches. As for the disbeliever, the angels descend upon him, and they stretch out their hands, 'al-bast' being striking, and they strike their faces and their backs at the time of death. When he is put into his grave, he is seated up, and it is said to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He does not return any answer to them, and Allah makes him forget the remembrance of that. When it is said: 'Who is the Messenger who was sent to you?' he is not guided to him and does not return any answer to it. Thus Allah leaves the wrongdoers astray."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi narrated to us, Shurayh ibn Maslamah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, from Amir ibn Sa'd al-Bajali, from Abu Qatadah al-Ansari, regarding the saying of the Most High: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [the verse], he said: "When the believer dies, he is made to sit in his grave, and it is said to him: 'Who is your Lord?' He says: 'Allah.' It is said to him: 'Who is your Prophet?' He says: 'Muhammad ibn Abdullah.' This is said to him several times. Then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'Look at your place in the Fire, had you turned away [[In T: "had you desired".]].' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'Look at your place in Paradise, since you stood firm.' When the disbeliever dies, he is made to sit in his grave, and it is said to him: 'Who is your Lord? Who is your Prophet?' He says: 'I do not know; I used to hear people saying.' It is said to him: 'You did not know.' Then a door to Paradise is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'Look at your place, had you stood firm' [[Addition from T and A.]], then a door to the Fire is opened for him, and it is said to him: 'Look at your place in the Fire, since you turned away' [[In T and A: "since you desired".]]. That is the saying of the Most High: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾."

Abd al-Razzaq said, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, regarding ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world﴾: "It is 'There is no god but Allah.' And ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ is the questioning in the grave." [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (1/296).]]

Qatadah said: As for ﴿the life of this world﴾, He keeps them firm with goodness and righteous deeds, and ﴿and in the Hereafter﴾ means in the grave. Similarly, this has been related from more than one of the early generations (salaf).

Abu Abdullah al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi said in his book Nawadir al-Usul: My father narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Nafi' narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Fudayk, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah [[In al-Tadhkirah: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah".]], from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to us one day while we were in the Mosque of Madinah, and he said: "Last night I saw something strange. I saw a man from my ummah [when the Angel of Death came to seize his soul, his kindness to his parents came to him and turned him back. And I saw a man from my ummah] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tadhkirah.]] over whom the punishment of the grave had been spread, and his ablution came to him and rescued him from that. And I saw a man from my ummah [who had been] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tadhkirah.]] surrounded by devils, and the remembrance of Allah came to him and freed him from among them. And I saw a man from my ummah surrounded by angels of punishment, and his prayer came to him and rescued him from their hands. And I saw a man from my ummah panting with thirst, whenever he came to a basin he was prevented from it, and his fasting came to him and gave him drink and quenched him. And I saw a man from my ummah while the prophets were sitting in circles, and whenever he approached one circle they drove him away, and his ghusl from impurity came to him, took him by the hand, and seated him beside me. And I saw a man from my ummah [in front of whom] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tadhkirah.]] there was darkness, behind him darkness, to his right darkness, to his left darkness, above him darkness, and below him darkness, and he was bewildered in it. His Hajj and his 'Umrah came to him and brought him out of the darkness and admitted him into the light. And I saw a man from my ummah who spoke to the believers but they did not speak to him. The bond of kinship came to him and said: 'O assembly of believers, speak to him,' and they spoke to him. And I saw a man from my ummah who was protecting his face from the heat or the sparks of the Fire with his hand, and his charity came to him and became a veil over his face and a shade over his head. And I saw a man from my ummah whom the guards of Hell had seized from every place, and his enjoining of good and forbidding of evil came to him and rescued him from their hands and admitted him among the angels of mercy. And I saw a man from my ummah kneeling on his knees, with a veil between him and Allah, and his good character came to him, took him by the hand, and brought him into the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And I saw a man from my ummah whose record had fallen from his left side, and his fear of Allah came to him, took his record, and placed it in his right hand. [And I saw a man from my ummah whose scale was light, and his children who had died before him came to him and made his scale heavy] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tadhkirah.]]. And I saw a man from my ummah standing at the edge of Hell, and his fear of Allah came to him and rescued him from that and he passed on. And I saw a man from my ummah who had fallen into the Fire, and his tears which he had shed out of fear of Allah in the world came to him and drew him out of the Fire. [And I saw a man from my ummah standing on the Sirat, trembling as a palm frond trembles, and his good opinion of Allah came and calmed his trembling, and he passed on.] [[Addition from T, A, and al-Tadhkirah.]] And I saw a man from my ummah on the Sirat, crawling at times and crawling on his hands and knees at other times, and his prayer upon me came to him, took him by the hand, raised him up, and he passed on over the Sirat. And I saw a man from my ummah who reached the gates of Paradise, and the gates were closed before him, and the testimony that there is no god but Allah came to him, and the gates were opened for him, and it admitted him into Paradise."

[[Al-Zabidi mentioned it in al-Ithaf and attributed it to al-Hakim in Nawadir, and weakened it. Al-Kharaiti narrated it in Makarim al-Akhlaq (no. 49) by way of Sa'id ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah, as a marfu' report, shorter than this. He mentioned that Ibn Taymiyyah used to greatly esteem this hadith and say: "It has supporting evidence for its soundness."]]

Al-Qurtubi said, after quoting this hadith by this route: "This is a great hadith, in which he mentioned specific deeds that save from specific terrors." He cited it thus in his book al-Tadhkirah. [[Al-Tadhkirah fi Ahwal al-Mawta wa Umur al-Akhirah (pp. 240–242).]]

The hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili has narrated in this regard a lengthy, strange hadith. He said: Abu Abdullah [[In A: "Abu Abd al-Rahman".]] Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Nukri narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr al-Bursani Abu Uthman narrated to us, Abu Asim al-Habati narrated to us, and he was among the best people of Basra, and was among the companions of Hazm and Sallam ibn Abi Muti', narrated to us Bakr ibn Khunays, from Dirar ibn Amr, from Yazid al-Raqashi, from Anas ibn Malik, from Tamim al-Dari, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Angel of Death: 'Go to My friend and bring him to Me, for I have tested him with ease and hardship, and I found him where I love him. Bring him to Me, for I will give him rest [[In T and A: "I will give him rest."]].'"

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 14, verse 27 (part 4 of 5):

Then the Angel of Death sets out toward him, and with him are five hundred angels. With them are shrouds and hanut (an aromatic embalming mixture) from Paradise, and with them are bundles of basil (rayhan). The root of the basil is one, but at its top are twenty colours, each colour having a scent different from the scent of the others. With them is white silk containing the strongest musk (al-misk al-adhfar). Then the Angel of Death sits at his head, and the angels surround him. Each angel places his hand on one of his limbs, and they spread that white silk and the strong musk beneath his chin. A door to Paradise is opened for him, and his soul then becomes distracted by a glimpse of Paradise at one moment, by its spouses at another, by its garments at another, and by its fruits at another, just as a child is distracted by his family when he cries." He said: "Indeed his spouses (in Paradise) rejoice at that with a joyful eagerness."

He said: "And the soul leaps." Al-Barsani said: "He means that it wants to leave in haste towards what it loves." He said: "And the Angel of Death says: 'Come out, O good soul, to lote-trees without thorns (sidr makhdud), and to acacia trees laden with fruit (talh mandud), and to extended shade, and to water poured forth.'" He said: "The Angel of Death is far gentler with him than a mother is with her child. He knows that this soul is beloved to its Lord, so he seeks with his gentleness to show affection to it, seeking the Lord's pleasure with him. Thus his soul is drawn out as a hair is drawn out of dough."

He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Those whom the angels take in death while they are good﴾ [An-Nahl: 32], and He says: ﴿As for if he was among those brought near (to Allah), then rest and provision and a Garden of pleasure﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 88-89]." He said: "Rest (rawh) is from the side of death, provision (rayhan) is what he is welcomed with, and a Garden of pleasure is what meets him."

He said: "When the Angel of Death seizes his soul, the soul says to the body: 'May Allah reward you on my behalf with good, for you were quick to take me to the obedience of Allah and slow to take me to the disobedience of Allah. You have been saved and you have saved.'" He said: "And the body says the same to the soul."

He said: "The places on earth where he used to obey Allah weep for him, and every gate of heaven through which his deeds ascended. And his provision descends (from there) for forty nights."

He said: "When the Angel of Death seizes his soul, five hundred angels stand by his body. No child of Adam turns him to one side except that the angels have turned him before them, washed him, and shrouded him in shrouds before the shrouds of the children of Adam, and (applied) hanut before the hanut of the children of Adam. Two rows of angels stand from the door of his house to the door of his grave, meeting him with forgiveness (istighfar). At that, Iblis lets out a cry by which the bones of his body split apart." He said: "He says to his soldiers: 'Woe to you! How did this servant escape from you?' They say: 'Indeed, this was a servant protected (from sin).'"

He said: "When the Angel of Death ascends with his soul, Jibril meets him with seventy thousand angels, each bringing him good news from his Lord that differs from the good news of the others." He said: "When the Angel of Death reaches the Throne with his soul, the soul falls down in prostration." He said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says to the Angel of Death: 'Go with the soul of My servant and place it in lote-trees without thorns, acacia trees laden with fruit, extended shade, and water poured forth.'"

He said: "When he is placed in his grave, prayer comes to him and is on his right; fasting comes to him and is on his left; the Qur'an comes and is at his head; his walking to prayer comes and is at his feet; and patience comes and is at the side of the grave." He said: "Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, sends a bundle of punishment." He said: "It comes to him from his right, and prayer says: 'Keep away from him! By Allah, he never stopped (being devoted) throughout his entire life, and he has only now rested since he was placed in his grave.'" He said: "Then it comes to him from his left, and fasting says the same." He said: "Then it comes to him from the direction of his head, and the Qur'an and remembrance (dhikr) say the same." He said: "Then it comes to him from the direction of his feet, and his walking to prayer says the same. The punishment does not come at him from any direction seeking an opening, but it finds that the friend of Allah has taken his shield." He said: "At that, the punishment withdraws and leaves."

He said: "Patience says to the (other) deeds: 'As for me, what prevented me from attending to him myself is only that I looked at what you had. If you had failed, I would have been his companion. But since you have sufficed for him, I am his treasure at the Sirat and the Scales.'"

He said: "Allah sends two angels whose eyes are like flashing lightning, whose voices are like crashing thunder, whose fangs are like pointed spikes, and whose breaths are like flames. They tread upon their hair, and between the shoulder of each of them is a distance of such-and-such. Mercy and compassion have been removed from them. They are called Munkar and Nakir, and in the hand of each of them is a hammer which, if Rabi'ah and Mudar gathered together to lift it, they could not lift." He said: "They say to him: 'Sit up!' He sits up and sits upright. His shrouds fall to his waist." He said: "They say to him: 'Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?'"

He said: They (the Companions) said: "O Messenger of Allah, who can speak at that time, given what you describe of the two angels?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿Allah firmly establishes those who believe with the firm word in the life of this world and in the Hereafter, and Allah leads astray the wrongdoers, and Allah does what He wills﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

He said: "He says: 'My Lord is Allah alone, with no partner. My religion is Islam, which the angels followed. My Prophet is Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets.'" He said: "They say: 'You have spoken the truth.'" He said: "They then expand the grave for him: forty cubits (dhira') in front of him, forty cubits on his right, forty cubits on his left, forty cubits behind him, forty cubits above his head, and forty cubits below his feet." He said: "So they expand it for him to two hundred cubits."

Al-Barsani said: "I think it is: and forty cubits surround him."

He said: "Then they say to him: 'Look above you!' And there is an open door to Paradise. They say to him: 'O friend of Allah, this is your dwelling, since you obeyed Allah.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, joy reaches his heart at that moment, and it never recedes. Then it is said to him: 'Look beneath you!'" He said: "He looks beneath him, and there is an open door to Hell. They say: 'O friend of Allah, you have been saved from what was against you.'" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Joy reaches his heart at that moment, a joy that never recedes." He said: 'A'ishah said: "Seventy-seven doors to Paradise are opened for him, and its breeze and coolness reach him until Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, resurrects him."

And with the chain of narration mentioned earlier to the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Allah, the Exalted, says to the Angel of Death: 'Go to My enemy and bring him to Me, for I have extended his provision and made My blessings easy for him, yet he refused anything but disobedience to Me. Bring him to Me so that I may take vengeance upon him.'"

He said: "The Angel of Death sets out toward him in the most hideous form anyone has ever seen. He has twelve eyes, and with him is a spit of fire full of thorns, and with him are five hundred angels. With them are brass and coals from the coals of Hell, and with them are whips of fire, soft like the softness of whips, yet a blazing fire." He said: "The Angel of Death strikes him with that spit in a blow such that each thorn of that spit penetrates to the root of every hair, vein, and nail." He said: "Then he twists it violently." He said: "He then draws his soul out from the nails of his feet." He said: "He throws it into his heels. Then the enemy of Allah becomes intoxicated with a stupor, and the Angel of Death gives him relief." He said: "And the angels strike his face and back with those whips." He said: "Then the Angel of Death pulls him forcefully, drawing out his soul from his heels and throwing it into his knees. Then the enemy of Allah becomes intoxicated with a stupor, and the Angel of Death gives him relief." He said: "The angels strike his face and back with those whips." He said: "Then the Angel of Death wrenches him with a sudden jerk, drawing his soul from his knees and throwing it into his waist. The enemy of Allah becomes intoxicated with a stupor, and the Angel of Death gives him relief." He said: "The angels strike his face and back with those whips." He said: "He continues like this up to his chest, then like this up to his throat." He said: "Then the angels spread that brass and the coals of Hell beneath his chin." He said: "The Angel of Death says: 'Come out, O cursed, accursed soul, to scorching wind and boiling water, and to a shade of black smoke, neither cool nor pleasant.'"

He said: "When the Angel of Death seizes his soul, the soul says to the body: 'May Allah reward you on my behalf with evil, for you were quick to take me to the disobedience of Allah and slow to take me to the obedience of Allah. You have been destroyed and you have destroyed.'" He said: "The body says the same to the soul. The places on earth where he used to disobey Allah curse him, and the armies of Iblis go to him and give him the good news that they have brought a servant of the children of Adam to the Fire."

He said: "When he is placed in his grave, his grave is constricted upon him until his ribs interlock, so that the right enters the left and the left enters the right." He said: "Allah sends to him black serpents like the necks of camels, which seize his nose and the big toes of his feet and bite him until they meet in his middle."

He said: "Allah sends two angels whose eyes are like flashing lightning, whose voices are like crashing thunder, whose fangs are like pointed spikes, and whose breaths are like flames. They tread upon their hair, and between the shoulders of each of them is a distance of such-and-such. Mercy and compassion have been removed from them. They are called Munkar and Nakir, and in the hand of each of them is a hammer which, if Rabi'ah and Mudar gathered together to lift it, they could not lift." He said: "They say to him: 'Sit up!'" He said: "He sits up." He said: "His shrouds fall to his waist." He said: "They say to him: 'Who is your Lord? What is your religion? Who is your Prophet?' He says: 'I do not know.' They say: 'You did not know, and you did not recite.'" They then strike him with a blow whose sparks fly about his grave, and then they return." He said: "They say: 'Look above you!' He looks, and there is an open door from Paradise. They say: 'This is—O enemy of Allah—your dwelling, had you obeyed Allah.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, at that moment regret reaches his heart, a regret that never recedes."

He said: "They say to him: 'Look beneath you!' He looks beneath him, and there is an open door to the Fire. They say: 'O enemy of Allah, this is your dwelling, since you disobeyed Allah.'"

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, at that moment regret reaches his heart, a regret that never recedes."

Ibn Kathir said: And ʿĀʾishah said: "Seventy-seven doors (sabʿah wa-sabʿūn bāban) are opened for him to Hell, and there comes to him [from] its heat and its scorching winds, until God sends him to it" [[Cited by Ibn Ḥajar in al-Maṭālib al-ʿĀliyah (4/382), attributing it to Abū Yaʿlā, who said: "This is a hadith of a strange (ʿajīb) context, and it bears witness to much of what is established in the long, well-known hadith of al-Barāʾ, but its chain is gharīb (singular) and contains weakness."]].

This is a very gharīb (singular, rarely transmitted) hadith with a remarkable (ʿajīb) wording. Yazīd al-Raqqāshī, who narrates it from Anas, has many gharāʾib (singular reports) and munkar (rejected) reports, and he is weak in narration according to the imams. And God knows best.

For this reason Abū Dāwūd said: Ibrāhīm ibn Mūsā al-Rāzī narrated to us: Hishām (that is, Ibn Yūsuf) narrated to us, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Baḥīr, from Hānīʾ, the freedman of ʿUthmān, from ʿUthmān, may God be pleased with him, who said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished burying a man, he would stand over him and say: 'Ask forgiveness for your brother, and ask for him steadfastness, for he is now being questioned.'" Abū Dāwūd alone reported it [[Sunan Abī Dāwūd, no. 3221.]].

The Ḥāfiẓ Abū Bakr ibn Mardawayh also reported, at God's words ﴿And if you could see when the wrongdoers are in the agonies of death, and the angels are stretching out their hands﴾ [al-Anʿām: 93], a very lengthy hadith from a strange route, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Ibn ʿAbbās, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), and it also contains gharāʾib.

I ask God to grant this book someone who will complete its verification, for it is among the greatest and most important books of tafsir. God is the One sought for help.]] Al-Bukhari said: His saying, ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief﴾, "Have you not known?" like His saying, ﴿Have you not seen how﴾ [Ibrahim: 24] and ﴿Have you not seen those who went out﴾ [al-Baqarah: 243]. Al-Bawar (ruin, destruction): destruction; "bara yaburu bawran" (it perished). And ﴿a people ruined (bur)﴾ [al-Furqan: 18; al-Fath: 12] meaning perishing.

Ali ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', who heard Ibn Abbas (recite): ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief﴾, and he said: "They are the disbelievers of the people of Makkah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4700).]]

Al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas concerning this verse: "It is Jabalah ibn al-Ayham and those among the Arabs who followed him, who joined the Romans." The well-known and authentic report from Ibn Abbas is the first statement, even though the meaning includes all disbelievers in general; for God Most High sent Muhammad ﷺ as a mercy to the worlds and a favor to mankind. Whoever accepts it and gives thanks for it enters Paradise, and whoever rejects it and disbelieves in it enters the Fire.

It has been narrated from Ali something similar to the first statement of Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

My father narrated to us, Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Abu al-Tufayl: that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali concerning ﴿those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin﴾, and he said: "The disbelievers of Quraysh on the Day of Badr."

Al-Mundhir ibn Shadhan narrated to us, Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, Bassam narrated to us — he is al-Sayrafi [[In T: "al-Sarafi".]] — from Abu al-Tufayl, who said: A man came to Ali and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, who are those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin?" He said: "The hypocrites of Quraysh."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Nufayl narrated to us, saying: I read to Ma'qil, from Ibn Abi Husayn [[In T, A: "Hunayn".]], who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, stood up and said: "Will no one ask me about the Qur'an? By Allah, if I knew today anyone more knowledgeable than me about it, even if he were beyond the seas, I would go to him." Then Abd Allah ibn al-Kawwa [[In T: "al-Kara'".]] stood up and said: "Who are those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin?" He said: "The polytheists of Quraysh; the favor of Allah came to them: faith, so they exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin."

Al-Adawi said concerning His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief﴾ and the rest of the verse, Muslim mentioned in full [[In A: "al-Masuf".]] from Ali that he said: "They are the two most wicked families of Quraysh: the Banu Umayyah and the Banu al-Mughirah. As for the Banu al-Mughirah, they caused their people to alight in the house of ruin on the Day of Badr, and as for the Banu Umayyah, they caused their people to alight in the house of ruin on the Day of Uhud. Abu Jahl was at Badr, and Abu Sufyan at Uhud. As for the house of ruin, it is Jahannam."

Ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us, al-Harith ibn Mansur narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: "I heard Ali recite this verse: ﴿and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin﴾," and he said: "They are the two most wicked families of Quraysh: the Banu Umayyah and the Banu al-Mughirah. As for the Banu al-Mughirah, they were destroyed on the Day of Badr, and as for the Banu Umayyah, they were given enjoyment for a time."

Abu Ishaq narrated it similarly from Amr ibn Murrah, from Ali, and it has been narrated through other chains from him.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Sa'd, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, concerning His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief﴾, he said: "They are the two most wicked families of Quraysh: the Banu al-Mughirah and the Banu Umayyah. As for the Banu al-Mughirah, you were sufficed against them on the Day of Badr, and as for the Banu Umayyah, they were given enjoyment for a time."

Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated similarly from Amr ibn Murrah, who said: Ibn Abbas said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: "O Commander of the Faithful, this verse: ﴿Those who exchanged the favor of Allah for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the house of ruin﴾," and he said: "They are the two most wicked families of Quraysh: my maternal uncles and your paternal uncles. As for my maternal uncles, Allah uprooted them on the Day of Badr, and as for your paternal uncles, Allah granted them respite for a time."

Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and Qatadah ibn Zayd [[In T: "Qatadah and Ibn Zayd".]] said: They are the disbelievers of Quraysh who were killed on the Day of Badr. Malik also narrated this in his Tafsir from Nafi', from Ibn Umar.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they set up rivals to Allah in order to mislead from His path﴾, meaning: they set up partners for Him, worshipped them alongside Him, and called the people to that.

Then He said, threatening them and warning them through the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾

That is: whatever you are able to do in this world, do it; whatever the case may be, ﴿your destination is the Fire﴾, meaning your return and your refuge is to it, as He said: ﴿We grant them enjoyment for a little, then We will drive them to a severe punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24], and He said: ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 70].

As for His saying: ﴿And they set up rivals to Allah in order to mislead from His path﴾, meaning: they set up partners for Him, worshipped them alongside Him, and called the people to that.

Then He said, threatening them and warning them through the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿Say: "Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire."﴾

That is: whatever you are able to do in this world, do it; whatever the case may be, ﴿your destination is the Fire﴾, meaning your return and your refuge is to it, as He said: ﴿We grant them enjoyment for a little, then We will drive them to a severe punishment﴾ [Luqman: 24], and He said: ﴿A brief enjoyment in this world; then to Us is their return; then We will make them taste the severe punishment because they used to disbelieve﴾ [Yunus: 70].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

Allah, the Exalted, says, commanding His servants to obey Him, to fulfil His right, and to show kindness to His creation: that they should establish the prayer, which is the worship of Allah alone with no partner, and that they should spend from what Allah has provided for them, by paying the zakat, spending on relatives, and being kind to strangers.

The meaning of establishing it is: observing its times and its prescribed limits, and its bowing, its humility and its prostrations.

Allah, the Exalted, commanded spending from what He has provided, secretly (fi al-sirr), that is, in privacy, and openly (al-'alaniyah), which is public giving. Let them hasten to do so for the salvation of their souls, ﴿before there comes a Day﴾, which is the Day of Resurrection, a Day ﴿in which there is no trade nor friendship﴾, meaning that no ransom will be accepted from anyone by which he could buy back his own soul, as Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Hadid: 15].

As for His words, ﴿nor friendship (khilal)﴾, Ibn Jarir said: it means there is no companionship of a friend, so that one would overlook the punishment of one who deserves it because of his friendship; rather, there is justice and equity there. Khilal is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker, "I befriended so-and-so (khallaltu fulanan), so I befriend him (ukhalluhu) with friendship and khilal (mukhalla wa khilal)." From this is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:

*I turned my desire away from them out of fear of destruction... and I am not one who dislikes khilal nor one who says it.*

Qatadah said: Allah knows that in this world there are trades and friendships by which people befriend one another in this world. A man looks at whom he befriends and whose companion he is; if it was for the sake of Allah, he should persist in it, and if it was for other than Allah, it will be cut off from him.

I say: The meaning of this is that Allah, the Exalted, informs that neither trade nor ransom benefits anyone, even if one were to ransom himself with the whole earth full of gold, should he find it; nor does anyone's friendship or anyone's intercession benefit him if he meets Allah as a disbeliever. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And fear a Day when no soul will avail another at all, nor will compensation be accepted from it, nor will intercession benefit it, nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Baqarah: 123], and Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided you before there comes a Day in which there is no trade, nor friendship, nor intercession. And the disbelievers are the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Baqarah: 254].

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 14, verses 32–34:

Allah enumerates His blessings upon His creation: He made the heavens a protected canopy [in A: "raised"]. He made the earth a bed, and He sent down water from the sky and brought forth by it pairs of diverse plants, including fruits and crops, varying in colors, shapes, tastes, scents and benefits. He subjected the ship by making it float upon the currents of the sea, running upon it by the command of Allah, the Exalted. He subjected the sea, carrying the ships, so that travelers might cross by them from one region to another, bringing what is here to there and what is there to here. He subjected the rivers, cutting through the earth from one land to another, as provision for the servants, for drinking, irrigation and other kinds of benefit.

﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both constant (in their courses)﴾, meaning: they move continuously and do not cease, by night or by day. ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outpace the day, and each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Yasin: 40]. ﴿He covers the night over the day, pursuing it swiftly, and (He created) the sun and the moon and the stars subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command; blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]. So the sun and the moon alternate, and the night and the day oppose each other: at times one takes from the other so that it lengthens, then the other takes from it so that it shortens. ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ [Luqman: 29]. Allah also said: ﴿He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a specified term﴾ [al-Zumar: 5].

As for His saying: ﴿And He gave you of all you asked of Him﴾, it means: He prepared for you everything you need in all your circumstances, of what you ask for according to your state and your speech [in T and A: "to your state"].

Some of the early generations (al-salaf) said: "of all you asked of Him and what you did not ask of Him."

Some reciters read: "wa-atakum min kulli ma sa'altumuhu" (with kull in the nominative).

As for His saying: ﴿And if you should count the favor of Allah, you could not enumerate them﴾, it informs of the inability of the servants to count the blessings, let alone to give thanks for them. As Talq ibn Habib, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The right of Allah is too heavy for the servants to fulfil, and the blessings of Allah are too many for the servants to count. But rise in the morning repentant and retire in the evening repentant."

In Sahih al-Bukhari, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, to You belongs all praise, a praise that is not repaid, nor abandoned, nor dispensed with, our Lord" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5458, from the hadith of Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him].

The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: Isma'il ibn Abi al-Harith narrated to us, Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us, Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Zayd al-'Abdi, from Anas, from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three registers will be brought out for the son of Adam on the Day of Resurrection: a register containing his righteous deeds, a register containing his sins, and a register containing the blessings of Allah upon him. Allah will say to the smallest of His blessings [in T and A: "to the smallest of them"] – I think he said – 'Into the register of blessings: take your price from his righteous deeds.' So it will exhaust all his righteous deeds, then it will withdraw and say: 'By Your might, I have not been fully compensated.' The sins and blessings will remain [in T and A: 'and the blessings and the righteous deeds, so his righteous deeds will be exhausted entirely']. When Allah wills to show mercy, He will say: 'O My servant, I have multiplied your good deeds for you and overlooked your evil deeds' – I think he said – 'and I have granted you My blessings.'" [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 3444, Kashf al-Astar, in which are Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar and Salih al-Murri, both weak narrators]. It is gharib, and its chain is weak.

It has been reported in an athar that Dawud (peace be upon him) said: "O Lord, how can I thank You when my thanks is itself a blessing from You upon me?" Allah the Exalted said: "Now you have thanked Me, O Dawud" – meaning: when you acknowledged your shortcoming in fulfilling the thanks due for blessings.

Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Praise belongs to Allah, who is such that the thanks for no blessing of His can be rendered except by a further blessing, which makes obligatory upon the one who renders thanks for past blessings a new blessing that makes obligatory upon him further thanks for it" [al-Risalah of al-Shafi'i, pp. 7–8].

Someone said on this matter:

"If every limb of mine had a tongue
that praised You for the goodness You bestowed,
then what my thanks had added, when I gave thanks with it,
would be more eloquent to You in gratitude and in favor."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) says, in this passage, arguing against the polytheists of Arabia: the Sacred City, Makkah, was founded first for the worship of Allah alone, with no partner. Ibrahim (peace be upon him), through whom it was made populated and inhabited, disassociated himself from those who worshipped other than Allah. He also supplicated for Makkah's security, saying: ﴿My Lord, make this city secure﴾. Allah answered him, as He says: ﴿Do they not see that We have made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 67]. He also says: ﴿Indeed, the first House established for mankind is that at Bakkah, blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs: the standing place of Ibrahim; and whoever enters it is secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 96-97]. In this story He says: ﴿My Lord, make this city secure﴾, so He defined it, as if he supplicated for it after its construction. Therefore He said: ﴿Praise be to Allah, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Ishaq﴾ [Ibrahim: 39]. It is known that Isma'il was thirteen years older than Ishaq. As for when he took Isma'il and his mother, while he was a suckling, to the place of Makkah, he also supplicated, saying: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 126], as we have mentioned there in Surat al-Baqarah in detail and at length.

And he said: ﴿And keep me and my sons away from worshipping idols﴾. It is fitting for every caller (to Allah) to supplicate for himself, his parents, and his offspring.

Then he mentioned that many people had been seduced by the idols, and that he was free of those who worshipped them, and he referred their affair to Allah: if He wills, He punishes them, and if He wills, He forgives them. This is like what Isa (peace be upon him) said: ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 118]. There is nothing in this beyond referring the matter to the will of Allah the Exalted, not an assertion that this (punishment) will occur.

Abdullah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us, that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abdullah ibn Amr, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the words of Ibrahim: ﴿My Lord, indeed they have led many people astray. So whoever follows me, he is of me; and whoever disobeys me, indeed You are Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and the words of Isa (peace be upon him): ﴿If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾. Then he raised his hands and said: "O Allah, my ummah! O Allah, my ummah! O Allah, my ummah!" and wept. Allah said: "O Jibril, go to Muhammad, and your Lord knows best, and ask him what makes him weep." So Jibril came to him and asked him, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) informed him of what he had said. Allah said: "Go to Muhammad and say to him: 'Indeed, We will please you concerning your ummah, and We will not grieve you.'" [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (13/151).]

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah Ibrahim (14), verses 42–43:

He, exalted is His majesty, says: "And do not think that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do," O Muhammad. That is: do not suppose that when He gives them respite and grants them a term, He is heedless of them or leaves them neglected, not punishing them for their deeds. Rather, He counts those deeds against them and records them precisely, "He only delays them for a Day when eyes will stare fixedly," that is, because of the intensity of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection.

Then He mentioned how they will rise from their graves and come to the place of assembly, saying: "Hurrying forward" (muhti'in), that is, rushing, as He said: "Rushing forward toward the caller; the disbelievers will say, 'This is a difficult day'" [al-Qamar: 8]. He also said: "On that day they will follow the caller, there will be no deviation from him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper" [Ta-Ha: 108], up to His words: "And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer, and he will have failed who carries injustice" [Ta-Ha: 111]. And He said: "On the Day they emerge from the graves swiftly, as if they were rushing to a target, racing" [al-Ma'arij: 43].

* *

As for His words, "with their heads raised" (muqni'i ru'usihim), Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid and others said: raising their heads.

"Their gaze will not return to them" (la yartaddu ilayhim tarfuhum): that is, rather their eyes will be fixed, staring, never blinking for an instant, because of the great terror, dread and fear of what will befall them. We seek refuge in Allah the Mighty from that. Hence He said: "And their hearts will be void" (wa af'idatuhum hawa'), that is, their hearts will be empty and hollow, containing nothing, due to the intensity of fright and dread and fear. For this reason Qatadah and a group said: the places of their hearts are empty, because the hearts have reached the throats, having left their places from the severity of fear. Some said: "hawa'" means a void, a thing that does not comprehend anything.

Because of the severity of what Allah the Exalted has told us about them, He said to His Messenger: "And warn the people of the Day when the punishment will come to them."

It is only a word he is saying, and behind them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 99-100]. Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman [ibn Dabil] [[Added from T; in A: "ibn Danyal".]] that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said about this verse: ﴿And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾. He said: That one who argued with Abraham about his Lord took two small eagles, and raised them until they became thick and strong and grew up. [[In T: "fa-shabba".]]

He said: He tied the leg of each of them with a stake to a chest, and starved them, and he and another man sat in the chest. He said: [He raised in the chest a stick at his head, with meat on it]. He said: Then they flew, and he began saying to his companion: "Look, what do you see?" He said: "I see such and such," until he said: "I see the whole world as if it were a fly." He said: Then he said: "Lower the stick," so he lowered it, and they descended. He said: So that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." Abu Ishaq said: And likewise it is in the recitation (qira'ah) of 'Abd Allah: "wa-in kada makruhum" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/160). "Sawwab al-'asa" means: he lowered it and brought it down. I say: It is likewise narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they recited: "wa-in kada," as 'Ali recited. Likewise it is narrated from 'Ikrimah that the context of this story is about Nimrod, king of Canaan: that he attempted to reach the means of the heavens by this trick and deception, just as after him Pharaoh, king of the Copts, attempted that in building the tower, and both failed and were weakened. They were the lesser, the more contemptible, the smaller and the more repelled.

Mujahid mentioned this story about Bukhtanassar (Nebuchadnezzar), and that when his sight was cut off from the earth and its people, it was called out: "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?" Shu'bah narrated from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman [ibn Dabil] [[Added from T; in A: "ibn Danyal".]] that 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said about this verse: ﴿And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾. He said: That one who argued with Abraham about his Lord took two small eagles, and raised them until they became thick and strong and grew up. [[In T: "fa-shabba".]]

He said: He tied the leg of each of them with a stake to a chest, and starved them, and he and another man sat in the chest. He said: [He raised in the chest a stick at his head, with meat on it]. He said: Then they flew, and he began saying to his companion: "Look, what do you see?" He said: "I see such and such," until he said: "I see the whole world as if it were a fly." He said: Then he said: "Lower the stick," so he lowered it, and they descended. He said: So that is the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it." Abu Ishaq said: And likewise it is in the recitation (qira'ah) of 'Abd Allah: "wa-in kada makruhum" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (13/160). "Sawwab al-'asa" means: he lowered it and brought it down. Taken from the margin of al-Shu'ab.]].

I say: It is likewise narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they recited: "wa-in kada," as 'Ali recited. Likewise, Sufyan al-Thawri and Isra'il narrated it from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Udhanan [[In T: "Arbab"; in A: "Aryan".]], from 'Ali, and mentioned something similar.

Likewise it is narrated from 'Ikrimah that the context of this story is about Nimrod, king of Canaan: that he attempted to reach the means of the heavens by this trick and deception, just as after him Pharaoh, king of the Copts, attempted that in building the tower, and both failed and were weakened. They were the lesser, the more contemptible, the smaller and the more repelled.

Mujahid mentioned this story about Bukhtanassar (Nebuchadnezzar), and that when his sight was cut off from the earth and its people, it was called out: "O tyrant, where do you intend to go?" So he was terrified; then he heard the voice above him, so he lowered the spears, and the eagles descended, and the mountains were frightened by their clamor, and the mountains nearly collapsed from the sound of that. [[In T: "min hin".]] That is the saying of Allah: ﴿And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾.

Ibn Juraij narrated from Mujahid that he recited it: "la-tazulu minhu al-jibal," with a fatha on the first lam and a damma on the second. [[In A and T: "wa-raf'" (and raising).]]

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾, that he said: Their plot was not such that the mountains would be moved by it. Likewise al-Hasan al-Basri said. Ibn Jarir gave it this interpretation: that what they did to themselves through their disbelief in Allah and their associating partners with Him did not harm the mountains or anything else; rather, the consequence of that returned upon themselves.

I say: This then resembles His saying: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed you will not tear the earth, nor will you reach the mountains in height﴾ [al-Isra': 37].

The second opinion in its interpretation: what 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And indeed their plot was such that the mountains would be moved by it﴾, he said: their shirk (associating partners with Allah), like His saying: ﴿The heavens are about to burst from it, and the earth split open, and the mountains collapse in ruin that they attribute to the Most Merciful a son﴾ [Maryam: 90-91]. Likewise said al-Dahhak and Qatadah.

Allah, the Exalted, says, affirming and emphasizing His promise: ﴿So do not think that Allah is one who would fail His promise to His messengers﴾, meaning: regarding their victory in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses stand.

Then He informs that He is Mighty (dhu 'izzah), that nothing He wills can resist Him or overpower Him, and that He is Avenger (dhu intiqam) against those who disbelieve in Him and deny Him: ﴿Woe on that Day to the deniers﴾ [al-Tur: 11]. For this reason He says: ﴿On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens [as well]﴾, meaning: this promise will be fulfilled on the Day when the earth is changed to another earth, and it will be [the earth] in a form other than its familiar and known attributes, as came in the Two Sahihs, from the hadith of Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection upon a white, pure land, like a loaf of fine bread, with no landmark in it belonging to anyone" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6521) and Sahih Muslim no. (2790)].

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Aishah that she said: "I was the first of the people to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about this verse: ﴿On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens; and they will come forth before Allah, the One, the Subduer﴾." She said: I said: "Where will the people be on that Day, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "On the Sirat (bridge)."

Ahmad also related it from 'Affan, from Wuhayb, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, from her (i.e., 'Aishah), and he did not mention Masruq [Musnad (6/134)].

He said: She said: "O Messenger of Allah, then where will the people be on that Day?" He said: "You have asked me about something that none of my Ummah has asked me about. Where will the people be on that Day, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "They will be on the back of Jahannam" [Musnad (6/117)].

Ibn Jarir said: al-Hasan narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Ja'd narrated to us, al-Qasim informed me, I heard al-Hasan say: 'Aishah said: "O Messenger of Allah, ﴿On the Day when the earth will be changed to another earth﴾, then where will the people be on that Day?" He said: "This is something that none has asked me about." He said: "On the Sirat, O 'Aishah."

Ahmad also related it from 'Affan, from al-Qasim ibn al-Fadl, from al-Hasan, with it [Tafsir al-Tabari (13/166) and Musnad (6/101)].

So I pushed him a push that nearly knocked him down. He said: 'Why do you push me?' I said: 'Will you not say: O Messenger of Allah?!' The Jew said: 'We only call him by the name his family gave him!' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'My name is Muhammad, the name my family gave me.' The Jew said: 'I came to ask you.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Will it benefit you if I tell you?' He said: 'I will listen with my ears.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) tapped the ground with a stick he had with him and said: 'Ask.' The Jew said: 'Where will the people be on the Day when the earth is changed to another earth, and the heavens?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'They will be in darkness, beyond the bridge.' He said: 'I will listen with my ears.' He said: 'I came to ask you about the child.' He said: 'The man's fluid is white and the woman's fluid is yellow. He said: I think he said: "Standing, until the sweat bridles them."

It was also narrated by another route from Shu'bah, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Amr ibn Maymun, from Ibn Mas'ud, similarly. And 'Asim narrated it likewise, from Zirr, from Ibn Mas'ud, with it.

Al-A'mash said, from Khaythamah, who said: 'Abdullah — that is, Ibn Mas'ud — said: "The whole earth on the Day of Resurrection will be fire, and the Garden behind it; you will see its maidens and its cups, and the sweat will bridle the people, or the sweat will reach them, and they will not yet have reached the reckoning."

Al-A'mash also said, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Qays ibn al-Sakan, who said: 'Abdullah said: "The whole earth on the Day of Resurrection is fire, and the Garden is behind it; you see its cups and its maidens. By Him in whose hand is the soul of 'Abdullah, a man will sweat so profusely that his foot sinks into the earth, then he rises until it reaches his nose, and the reckoning has not touched him." They said: "From what is that, O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman?" He said: "From what people see of what they will meet."

(2489); its wording is: "Indeed beneath the sea is fire, and beneath the fire is sea," narrated through Bishr Abu 'Abdullah from Bashir ibn Muslim from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr marfu'an; a group of imams weakened this hadith. See their statements in al-Silsilah al-Da'ifah no. (478)].

Then Allah will drive the creation with one driving, and behold, they will be upon this changed earth" [its takhrij was previously mentioned in the tafsir of Surah al-An'am].

His saying: ﴿And they will come forth before Allah﴾, meaning: all the creatures will come out of their graves before Allah, ﴿the One, the Subduer﴾, meaning: the One who has subdued everything and overcome it, to whom necks submit and minds are humbled.

Allah says: ﴿On the day when the earth will be changed to another earth, and the heavens as well﴾, and the creatures will come forth before their Lord (Dayyan). ﴿O Muhammad, you will see that day the criminals﴾, namely those who committed crimes through their disbelief and corruption, ﴿bound together in chains﴾. So they brought back the garments and the captives, and we returned with kings in shackles.

This Qur'an is a message (balagh) for mankind, as He says: ﴿so that I may warn you thereby, and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19], meaning: it is a message for all of creation, both humans and jinn, just as He said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Alif, Lam, Ra. This is a Book which We have sent down to you, that you may bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by the permission of their Lord﴾.

﴿And that they may be warned thereby﴾, i.e., that they may take heed (yatta'idhu) by it. ﴿And that they may know that He is but one God﴾, i.e., that they may derive proof from the arguments and indications it contains that there is no god but Him. ﴿And that those of understanding may be reminded﴾, i.e., those possessing intellects.
